name: Bina (Nigeria)
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: OLAC resources in and about the Bina language [byj] (Wayback capture Dec 2024)
sources.note: Lists only Glottolog, Ethnologue and LINGUIST List entries; no descriptive resource.

sources.citation: University of Ilorin 2011 B.A. long essays, Dept. of Linguistics and Nigerian Languages (07/15CB series; 70 Wayback captures of unilorin.edu.ng/studproj/arts/, text-searched)
sources.note: No essay on Bina exists in the captured series (neighbouring Kono, Kurama, Atsam, Kuturmi are covered). Not saved under bina1270.

sources.citation: Aliyu, Usman. 2026. An analysis of negative polar questions in Bina language: a Government and Binding approach. Jalingo Journal of Multi-Disciplinary Research and Innovations (JAJMURI) 2(1), March 2026, 8 pp. ISSN 3093-0243. https://oer.tsuniversity.edu.ng/index.php/jajmuri/article/view/2008
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Describes a tonal question morpheme: negative yes/no questions copy 'the last vowel of the final syllable... plus a low tone which serves as a question morpheme' (p.4; summary p.7). Cites the unpublished primary works: Aliyu 2024 BUK PhD thesis, Aliyu & Yalwa 2024, Aliyu 2025.

sources.citation: Usman, Aliyu & Hammed Salami. 2025. Government and Binding approach to interrogative construction in Bina: a case of in-situ and ex-situ content questions. Sokoto Journal of Linguistics and Communication Studies (SOJOLICS) 1(1): 269-281. doi:10.36349/sojolics.2025.v01i01.032 (open PDF via sojolics.com / Google Drive)
sources.note: Nothing. Syntax paper (GB analysis of content questions, 16 speakers in Kauru LGA); all Bina data tone-marked; p.272 says content question words 'are assigned high tone... when echo-question... is targeted'. No word for stress/accent anywhere.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2020. The East Kainji languages of Central Nigeria. Afrika und Ubersee 93: 45-67. doi:10.15460/auue.2020.93.1.210
sources.note: Bin listed in Table 1 (p.48) as 'Vigorous', source 'Blench (2016)' = his own untranscribed/unpublished 2016 survey data; sec. 3.1 phonology discusses Boze tone and Shimizu's H/L transcriptions only; Bin absent even from the Table 12 comparanda. Nothing on Bin phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2019. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, edition IV. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. Entry 48 'Bin'.
sources.note: Entry gives names (Bina, tiBin, biBin pl. aBin, Binawa, Bogana), location (Saminaka/Kauru LGA), ca. 3-4000 speakers (2016 est.), and 'Wordlist: Blench (2016)' as the only linguistic source. Nothing on phonology.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Stuart McGill. 2012. The Kainji languages of northwestern and central Nigeria. Circulation draft, 369 pp.
sources.note: States 'Many languages, especially of the Kauru group, appear to have no material available at all'; Bina only in the classification list. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2004/2012 ms. The East Kainji languages of Central Nigeria: state of the art. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation, 12 pp.
sources.note: Bina appears only in the Kauru subgroup list (pp.10-11) with empty data cells; nothing on its phonology.

sources.citation: Aliyu, Usman. 2025. Interrogative constructions: the example of yes/no questions in Bina of Kaduna State. KADA Journal of Liberal Arts 16(1). Kaduna: Kaduna State University.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Per Aliyu 2026 it treats the prosodic (tonal) marking of yes/no questions in Bina; may contain a fuller note on the tone system.

sources.citation: Aliyu, Usman & Lawan D. Yalwa. 2024. Interaction between the content word question (CQW) and focus construction in Bina language. Bayero Journal of Linguistics 10(2): 1-15.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Companion article from the thesis; possible language-background section with tone/syllable notes.

sources.citation: Aliyu, Usman. 2024. An analysis of question formation in Bina language. PhD thesis, Department of Linguistics and Foreign Languages, Bayero University, Kano.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Only substantial modern first-hand study of Bina (tiBin); Nigerian PhD theses on syntax routinely include a 'sound system' chapter (consonants, vowels, tone, syllable structure) where any stress/tone-language statement would sit. Source of the two open articles saved here.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger (with Luther Hon). 2016. Bin (tiBin) wordlist and survey notes, Kauru LGA, Kaduna State. Unpublished field data cited as 'Blench (2016)' in An Atlas of Nigerian Languages ed. IV (2019) entry 48 and in Blench 2020 (AuU 93) Table 1.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only lexical/phonetic documentation of Bina by a Kainji specialist; Blench's 'X language of Central Nigeria and its affinities' write-ups normally include a short phonology section with a tone statement.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2016. Bin [tiBin] wordlist / survey data (with Luther Hon, SIL Nigeria). Unpublished field materials cited as 'Blench (2016)' in Blench 2019 Atlas and Blench 2020.
sources.note: Never posted on rogerblench.info (Wayback CDX of the East Kainji directory shows no Bin file); not transcribed per Blench 2020 p.47.
